result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`, the tier explicitly declared at spawn. Declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-18 — the dock's "certified chrome ink" referent is read off `.glass-dock`, a node that paints nothing under Glass 7 (measured `rgba(0,0,0,0)` in both schemes; the paint is on the `.dock-plate` child, measured α 0.5392 light / 0.5776 dark). `resolveLiveTint` therefore returns `undefined` on every call and the static model it exists to distrust (α 0.80/0.88) serves every certification on the dock band, unnoticed since the W44 Glass 7 adoption. The mechanism is a demo feature module (`demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts:152`) reaching across two package boundaries into a producer-private DOM class by `document.querySelector` — the weakest coupling the language offers, for a value the producer already computes, serving exactly one consumer (`ProfileSection.vue:28`, the dock).
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, but three axes were checked and found sound and are recorded as such in the report: (1) no demo file reaches into `src/` or `dist/` — all 50 value.js import sites use published `package.json#exports` subpaths (`grep -rho '@mkbabb/value.js[a-z/]*' demo | sort | uniq -c` → 25 /color, 10 /css, 6 /math, 5 /easing, 4 /quantize, 1 bare inside a comment); Dock.vue imports the library not at all, correct for chrome. (2) `verbatimModuleSyntax` holds across the whole dock subtree, and it is load-bearing: because `Dock.vue:24`'s `import type { DockActionBar }` is erased, the dock's runtime graph is 65 modules rather than the 195 that `usePaneRouter` itself pulls (measured, L-graph2.mjs). (3) `main` = 1 and `nav` = 1 on 60/60 audit captures and live; the producer's inert/aria-hidden packaging of inactive dock faces is correct (measured `inert:true, visibility:hidden` at rest).

defects.defect: The chrome-tier ink referent probes a node that paints nothing: `resolveLiveTint("chrome")` reads `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.glass-dock')).backgroundColor`, which is fully transparent under Glass 7 — the glass is painted on the `.dock-plate` child. The live probe returns undefined on every call and the static model silently serves.
defects.evidence: demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts:150-153 (the querySelector) and :217 (`if (!resolved || resolved.alpha === 0) return undefined`). Measured live (scratchpad L-probe5.mjs, /#/, 1280x900, dock expanded): light {"dockBg":"rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)","plateBg":"color(srgb 0.931227 0.845921 0.816039 / 0.5392)"} ; dark {"dockBg":"rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)","plateBg":"color(srgb 0.390298 0.334077 0.29024 / 0.5776)"}. Producer paint site: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dock/styles/morph.css `.glass-dock:not(.vertical) .dock-plate { background: color-mix(...) }`. Static fallback now in force: demo/color-session/ink.ts:29-35 RUNG_ALPHA.floating = {light 0.8, dark 0.88}, FLOATING_TINT_L = {light 1, dark 0.345}, applied to chrome at ink.ts:118-122. Sole consumer of the tier: `grep -rn 'useSafeAccentFn("chrome")' demo` -> demo/shell/dock/menus/ProfileSection.vue:28.
defects.mechanism: Cross-package boundary violation: a demo feature module reaches a producer's internal paint value through a DOM class-name query instead of a published token/contract. Untyped, unexported, untested — so a producer paint change (Glass 7, adopted whole at V·W44) un-wires it silently.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/L-probe5.mjs against the live dev server on localhost:9000 — prints dockBg rgba(0,0,0,0) and the real plateBg with alpha 0.5392/0.5776 in light/dark. Consequence example (labelled: assumed ambient L 0.75): surfaceLightness = a*L + (1-a)*ambient gives 0.95 modelled vs 0.83 measured — ink certified against a surface an eighth of the OKLab range too light. e2e/smoke/oracles/o18-contrast-census.spec.ts:594-635 measures only the outcome at one boot colour and never asserts the live probe returned anything.
defects.proposedCure: The referent is the producer's own composited value, so the producer publishes it: glass-ui exposes `--glass-tint-chrome` (resolved) or `useDockSurfaceTint()` on the existing DockContext, and the demo reads a token, never a node. The `chrome` branch — and the identical `querySelector('[data-surface="veil"]')` idiom at :170-176 — then collapse to token reads with no DOM archaeology. Interim `.glass-dock .dock-plate` is another line of the same wrong kind and will break on the next paint change. Secondary: the selector is document-order dependent — two `.glass-dock` elements exist on /#/atmosphere and /#/blob (demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:164); measured firstIsShell:true today, breakage on re-order is a hypothesis.

defects.defect: `isAdminMode` is a one-way latch defined by two disagreeing predicates. After one visit to a tuning route the dock wears admin identity (gold shimmer glyph + gold `--dock-ring`) on every subsequent non-admin route for the rest of the session.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/composables/useDockAdminMode.ts:32 seeds the ref with a PREFIX test `currentView.startsWith("admin-")`; :55-59 maintains it with a MEMBERSHIP test `adminViews.includes(view)` and has no falsifying arm. The two predicates disagree on `atmosphere`/`blob` (in the array at :27, not prefixed). Reproduced live (scratchpad L-probe6.mjs, headless Chromium 1280x900): `1 fresh picker {"route":"#/","goldIcon":false,"ring":"oklch(0.471189 0.188448 9.8340"}` / `2 -> atmosphere {"goldIcon":true,"ring":"light-dark(oklch(0.751 0.147 8"}` / `3 back() -> picker {"route":"#/","goldIcon":true,"ring":"light-dark(oklch(0.751 0.147 8"}` / `4 -> palettes {"goldIcon":true,...}`.
defects.mechanism: Duplicated state for a value that is a pure function of the route, with the predicate implemented twice and neither copy owned by the schema that owns views (demo/shell/viewSchema.ts).
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/L-probe6.mjs — load /#/ (gold false), hash to /#/atmosphere (gold true), page.goBack() to /#/ (gold STILL true), hash to /#/palettes (gold STILL true). With admin credentials the damage is functional, not cosmetic: viewEntries (:34-39) then returns only the seven admin views while on /#/palettes, so the dock's own navigation cannot reach the user views except through the `__admin_toggle__` sentinel row.
defects.proposedCure: Derive, do not latch. Add `group: "user" | "admin"` to `PaneConfig` (viewSchema.ts owns the partition) and reduce the composable to `const isAdminMode = computed(() => VIEW_MAP[viewManager.currentView.value].group === "admin")`. The ref, both watchers and both hardcoded ViewId arrays die; `toggleAdminMode` keeps its real job (it navigates) and the flag follows the route by construction — the same transposition `useViewManager.ts:51-58` already applied to `mobilePaneIndex`.

defects.defect: The local `useLayerTransition` shim in ActionBarLayer produces no crossfade at all: the producer CSS the template hand-binds declares no opacity transition, so the 260 ms timer window is an instant cut with a transparent inert box held over the live controls.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue:62-94 (the shim, SUB_LAYER_CROSSFADE_MS = 260, subLayerProps hand-binding `.dock-layer`/`is-active`/`is-leaving`). Producer rules: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dock/styles/layers.css declares only `transition: visibility 0s linear var(--duration-normal)` on `.dock-layer`; the opacity overlap lives on `.dock-crossfade[data-crossfading] > .dock-face` via `--dock-t` (crossfade.css), reachable only inside `<DockCrossfade>`. Measured live (scratchpad L-probe2.mjs), both faces at rest / +60ms / +460ms across the actions->input swap: `transitionProperty: "visibility", transitionDuration: "0s"` at every phase; opacity steps 1->0 and 0->1 in one frame; the leaving face holds a 442x45 transparent inert box. The public successor exists: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dock/index.d.ts:5 `export { default as DockCrossfade } from "./DockCrossfade.vue";` — contradicting the shim's own comment at ActionBarLayer.vue:54-61.
defects.mechanism: A local fork of a retired producer concept, styled out of the producer's private stylesheet by class-name convention; the fork reimplements the packaging but cannot reach the animation, which the producer moved behind a component.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/L-probe2.mjs — navigate /#/, click [aria-label='Toggle action bar'], click [aria-label='Open color input'], sample getComputedStyle on both children of `.dock-layer-grid` at 60 ms and 460 ms. transition-property is `visibility` and duration `0s` in all four phases.
defects.proposedCure: Replace ActionBarLayer.vue:62-101 with `<DockCrossfade :active="activeSubLayer" reserve="inline">` wrapping two `<DockLayer id="actions">` / `<DockLayer id="input">` faces. The shim, the 260 ms literal, the timer, `subLayerProps`, `subLayerGridEl`, the `void opts.containerEl` parity argument and the hand-bound producer classes all die (~40 lines), and the producer's spring-driven overlap, peak-size reserve and focus transfer from a dissolving face arrive instead of being approximated.

Extend the existing owner rather than adding one: `useDocumentTitle` becomes `useDocumentIdentity(route)` returning `{ title, heading }` from the same `viewSchema` row, the shell renders `

{{ heading }}

` as the first child of App.vue's `

defects.defect: The demo's declared view of the published library surface has drifted from `package.json#exports`: tsconfig.demo.json maps a nonexistent `dist/index.d.ts`, declares two subpaths that are not exported, and omits two that are — while calling itself a mirror of the generated Vite alias set.
defects.evidence: `package.json#exports` keys = ['./color','./value','./css','./easing','./math','./transform','./quantize'] — 7 keys, no '.' root. tsconfig.demo.json paths declare `@mkbabb/value.js` -> ./dist/index.d.ts (`ls dist/index*` -> no matches found), plus `/parsing` and `/units` (neither in exports; no src/subpaths/parsing.ts or units.ts — `ls src/subpaths` -> color, css, easing, math, quantize, transform, value), and omit `/value` and `/css` (both exported; `/css` used 10x in demo and 4x inside glass-ui's dist). The file's header calls this 'the 8 public keys' / 'a CLOSED 8-key set' that 'mirrors the vite.config.ts runtime self-alias generated from the same map'; vite.config.ts:41-50 generates one alias per exports entry -> 7 aliases and no bare-root alias.
defects.mechanism: A hand-maintained declaration of a generated surface: the runtime alias set is derived from exports, the type paths are not, so the two views of the public API drift silently.
defects.reproduction: NONE — latent, not live. No demo file imports the bare `@mkbabb/value.js` specifier (`grep -rn '@mkbabb/value.js"' demo` -> the only hit is prose at demo/shared/utils.ts:12), and glass-ui's three specifiers (/color, /css, /easing, measured in its dist) are all covered by the generated alias set, so one instance serves the running app. Were the bare specifier ever written it would resolve to node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0 — the published copy npm installed for glass-ui's peer dep — a second instance of this library behind an undeclared specifier.
defects.proposedCure: Generate the tsconfig `paths` from `package.json#exports` exactly as the Vite aliases already are (one loader, one source of truth), or add a real `"."` export plus `dist/index.d.ts`. Either way the two declarations of the public surface cannot drift apart again — this is the axis T.W1's dogfood keystone was fought over.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law) for demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m], 1M context) — the tier explicitly declared at spawn; seat declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — the only focus indicator on the app's primary text-entry control is `border-color: <the user's own selected colour, alpha included>` with the UA outline explicitly suppressed (`focus-visible:outline-none`, ColorInput.vue:16 + :162-166). Measured contrast against the field's own background rgb(251,250,248): #fbfaf8 → 1.00:1; white → 1.04:1; alpha 0 → fully transparent. WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 floor is 3:1. There is no forced-colors fallback either — the element matches NONE of foundation.css:702-720's focus-restoration roster (measured el.matches(roster) === false; role="textbox"/[contenteditable] are not in the roster and the element carries no tabindex attribute). And in the error state the destructive branch of `inputStyle` returns first, so the error border erases the focus border entirely. The bitter part: the app's certified contrast-safe accent (SAFE_ACCENT_KEY, computed from cssColorOpaque precisely so alpha cannot destroy contrast) IS injected in this same component at :157 — and is spent on the arrow glyph's stroke while the raw alpha-bearing cssColor takes the focus indicator.

defects.defect: Focus indicator is the user's raw alpha-bearing colour with the UA outline suppressed; measured contrast 1.00:1 for reachable colours; no forced-colors fallback; error state overwrites focus state.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue:16 (`focus-visible:outline-none`) and :162-166 (`if (inputIsFocused.value) return { borderColor: cssColor.value }`). Live after a real click: `focused: true, outline: "none 1px rgb(0,95,204)", inlineStyle: "border-color: lab(92 88.8 20 / 0.827);"`. Measured contrast vs the field's own measured background rgb(251,250,248): `#fbfaf8` → 1.00, `rgb(255 255 255)` → 1.04, `oklch(0.7 0.1 200 / 0)` → alpha 0 / invisible. Forced-colors roster membership measured via el.matches() against foundation.css:702-720: colorInput → false, sendBtn → true; colorInput attrs = [data-v-…, contenteditable, role, aria-label, class] (no tabindex). Error+focus measured inline style: `border-color: var(--destructive)`. Contrast-safe primitive available and unused for this purpose: demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts:273-292, injected at ColorInput.vue:157 and spent on the arrow stroke at :74/:81.
defects.mechanism: Accessibility-critical state expressed through a user-data-driven decorative channel with no floor, no fallback register, and no separation from a competing state — instead of a design-system focus register.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/ at >=1440px viewport → hover the dock → click `Tools` (aria-label="Toggle action bar") → click `Open color input` → drag the alpha channel slider to 0 (or set the colour to white in light mode) → click the field. Focus is undetectable. In WHCM the element matches no outline-restoration selector.
defects.proposedCure: Delete `focus-visible:outline-none` and the focus branch of `inputStyle` entirely. Focus comes from the house register — demo/styles/focus-ring.css / the `.focus-ring` class that four sibling dock controls measurably carry (measured siblingButtonsUsingFocusRing: 4, colorInput.usesFocusRing: false). Architecturally this dissolves by adopting glass-ui `Input`, which owns its own focus register. If the live colour must appear on this control it appears as a swatch, never as the focus boundary.

defects.defect: The parse-error affordance carries zero programmatic semantics and physically occludes 83% of the send button and 66% of the field it describes.
defects.evidence: Measured with the badge live on screen (frames/B-error-badge-over-send.png): badge left 682.1 right 783.1 width 101.0; send left 763.1 right 787.1 width 24.0 → overlap 20.0px = 83% of the button; input width 153.0 → badge covers 66% of the field. defects.mechanism: An error rendered as a floating decoration positioned against the same physical edge as the recovery action, instead of as a field state with an associated message region.
defects.reproduction: Open the colour input at >=1440px, focus it, and drive a stream of distinct invalid strings at ~2.6s intervals (e.g. `lab(#)`, `lab(##)`, …) so the 2s auto-clear never fires. defects.defect: ~2.04s trailing debounce before any feedback, no live preview while typing at human cadence, and complete silence when the same invalid string is retried.
defects.evidence: demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:92 `debounce(parseAndSetColor, 2000)`; :62 `if (!input || input === previousInvalid) return;`; :57 error auto-clears after 2000ms. Four measured live trials — T1 fresh `lab()` → badge at 2037ms; T2 SAME `lab()` retried → badge NEVER; T3 different `zzz(` → 2048ms; T4 `lab()` again after previousInvalid changed → 2041ms. Separately: driving the field at a 900ms cadence for 4s produced no badge at all, because every keystroke resets the 2000ms trailing timer.
defects.mechanism: A trailing debounce an order of magnitude past the interaction-feedback threshold, combined with a stale-input dedup cache guarding a pure function, and an error truth that lives only on a 2s timer.
defects.reproduction: At http://localhost:9000/#/ with the colour input open and focused: type `lab()` and wait — the badge appears at ~2.04s and vanishes 2s later. Now clear and type `lab()` again — nothing ever appears. Separately, type `oklch(0.7 0.1 200)` at roughly one character per second: zero live colour preview for the entire 18-character entry.
defects.proposedCure: Leading-edge debounce at ~120-200ms for the live preview; derive the error state from the current value so it PERSISTS while the value is invalid rather than flashing on a timer; delete `previousInvalid` entirely — it is a cache guarding a pure function and it is the mechanism that silences the natural human retry loop. PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-08 already rules this family ADD-AFFORDANCE.

defects.defect: Direction and bidi: every offset is physical, and the field renders a CSS-colour string with no LTR isolation.

defects.defect: The crown entrance animation never runs, on any device, in any browser, and never has. ColorInput.vue:36-39 binds `animation: crown-appear ...` in an INLINE style attribute; ColorInput.vue:369-376 defines `@keyframes crown-appear` inside `<style scoped>`. Vue's SFC compiler hash-suffixes scoped keyframe names and rewrites animation declarations within the same style block, but does NOT process template style attributes. The inline reference resolves to nothing. NEW this pass — it also refutes the first pass's negative proof line 654, 'The animation law is honoured.'
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue:38 (inline `animation: crown-appear var(--duration-panel) var(--ease-decelerate) forwards;`) vs :369 (`@keyframes crown-appear`). Compiled sheet served by the dev server: `curl -s "http://localhost:9000/@fs/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue?vue&type=style&index=0&scoped=55dadc03&lang.css"` → contains `@keyframes crown-appear-55dadc03 {...}` and, for contrast, the class-driven sibling correctly rewritten: `.color-input-mode-flash[data-v-55dadc03] { animation: input-mode-flash-55dadc03 ... }`. Live document keyframe census (all stylesheets, all CSSKeyframesRule names): {"exactCrownAppear": false, "crownLike": ["crown-appear-55dadc03"], "totalKeyframes": 54}. No global fallback: `grep -rn "crown-appear" demo/` returns exactly 3 hits — ColorInput.vue:38, ColorInput.vue:369, demo/DESIGN.md:213 (prose). demo/styles/animations.css does not contain it.
defects.mechanism: Wrong home for a keyframe, forced by a per-instance inline style. A scoped @keyframes is consumable only from a class rule in the same block; an inline style attribute is consumable only against a GLOBAL keyframe. Pairing the two is unsatisfiable by construction — no combination of the two halves can ever resolve. Violates edict 6 (an animation deleted by construction rather than by decision) and edict 5 (per-instance inline override where a root-level class belongs).
defects.reproduction: 1) `curl -s "http://localhost:9000/@fs/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue?vue&type=style&index=0&scoped=55dadc03&lang.css"` — observe the definition is emitted as `crown-appear-55dadc03`. 2) In any live page at http://localhost:9000, evaluate: `[...document.styleSheets].flatMap(s=>{try{return [...s.cssRules]}catch{return []}}).filter(r=>r.type===CSSRule.KEYFRAMES_RULE).map(r=>r.name).includes('crown-appear')` → false.
defects.proposedCure: crown-appear is a design-language beat, not seat geometry: promote it to demo/styles/animations.css (which already exists and is the declared home for global keyframes) and drive it from a `.crown-badge` CLASS. The inline style attribute dies with it. Adopt the rule repo-wide: if the reference is inline, the keyframe must be global; if the keyframe is scoped, the reference must be a class in the same block. No third combination is legal.

The discriminant is erased at every hop. Two further silencers compound it: `initialParse` (useColorParsing.ts:83) suppresses a composable's first failure, and `previousInvalid` (useColorParsing.ts:62) makes any REPEAT of the same string a total no-op — the state a frustrated user reaches within two seconds.

(2) It would not matter: the callee catches everything itself (`useSlugMigration.ts:74-88`) and dispatches onto `slugBarRef.value?.setError(...)`, a permanently-null ref. (3) `slugError` is written at six sites in SlugEditLayer and rendered at zero — the template contains no reference to it. And the substring branches at :59-62 are a verbatim resurrection of the exact bug `useSlugMigration.ts:77-82` records as killed at S.W2 W2-6 (`ApiProblem` does `super(title)`, so `e.message` is the server title and can never contain '409'/'404'/'429').

defects.defect: RTL: the @mbabb wordmark bidi-reorders to `mbabb@`, and the dock's two directional affordances (Tools ArrowRight / Back ArrowLeft) do not mirror, so the enter/exit motif is inverted wholesale.

VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6.1: 'CSS strings, hex, slugs, IDs and provenance render in LTR-isolated spans inside RTL prose'; 'chrome, navigation and layout follow logical inline/block direction'.
defects.mechanism: A handle beginning with '@' is a neutral-then-Latin run; in an RTL paragraph direction the neutral leading '@' resolves to the right of the Latin run. No dir="ltr"/unicode-bidi:isolate wrapper. Separately, the layer-swap affordance is drawn with physical arrow glyphs while its meaning ('forward into the layer' / 'back out') is logical.
defects.reproduction: Open docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/rtl-desktop/picker.png and read the dock band; or re-run states.mjs matrix rtl-desktop (documentElement.setAttribute('dir','rtl') post-load, per its MT-F022 fix #1).
defects.proposedCure: dir="ltr" / unicode-bidi:isolate on @mbabb and on the slug pill (same family — ProfileSection.vue:75, MobileMenuDropdown.vue:50). Replace the two physical arrows with one logical chevron primitive that flips with `direction`: there are exactly two instances and they must always agree, so they should be one component, not two icon imports.

defects.defect: Three visible dividers for four visible seats — a line between every adjacent pair — in a row where every one of those four items already draws its own capsule seat.

Sources: ProfileSection.vue:49 AND :123 (a separator on both sides of the auth block), ActionBarToggle.vue:82. PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-05 terminal verb REMOVE/KEEP and §5 law 4: 'A divider is retained only when grouping would be ambiguous without it. Spacing plus material already expressing the same boundary makes the line duplicative.'
defects.mechanism: Each dock sub-component ships its own DockSeparator as local furniture, so the count is the sum of independent decisions rather than one composition decision. The maximum possible duplication (n−1 lines for n seats) is reached exactly because no one owns the row.
defects.reproduction: node D-dock-probe5.mjs — count nav .dock-separator total vs those with rect>0 and not inside [inert], at 1440x900 on /#/.
defects.proposedCure: Zero dividers in the main layer; the capsule seats already group and the dock's own gap token supplies the rhythm. Separator ownership moves to the layer composition (Dock.vue), never to the leaf components — a leaf cannot know whether its boundary is ambiguous.

defects.defect: A dock layer swap jolts the pill 81px sideways and shrinks it 162px, unanimated — the persistent chrome jumps on a single click of Login.
defects.evidence: D-dock-probe3.mjs at 1440x900: main layer dock {x:484.3, w:471.5, h:62}; slug-edit layer dock {x:565.5, w:309.0, h:62}. Δx = +81.2px, Δw = −162.5px. glass-ui/dist/components/dock/styles/crossfade.css cross-fades opacity only ('.dock-crossfade > .dock-face {opacity:0} … .is-active {opacity:1}'), so the box change is instantaneous. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3 law 4: the dock owns a reserved band and its expanded/collapsed/mounted states do not move the scene.
defects.mechanism: GlassDock is instantiated with :fit-content="true" (Dock.vue:132) while hosting four DockLayers of very different intrinsic widths as grid-area:1/1 siblings. fit-content therefore tracks whichever layer is active, making the dock's inline size a property of the layer rather than of the dock.
defects.reproduction: node D-dock-probe3.mjs (matrix B) — 1440x900, goto /#/, read .glass-dock rect, click Login, wait, read .glass-dock rect again.
defects.proposedCure: The dock's inline size is a property of the dock. Either size the container to the max of its layers (they are already coincident grid siblings, so `grid-template-columns: max-content` over all faces gives it for free), or drive width on the producer's morph spring so the change is a motion rather than a jump. Drop :fit-content on a multi-layer dock.

defects.defect: The single layout-forcing animation in the dock is the one that fires on boot: the Tools presence slot transitions grid-template-columns, and it uses a duration/ease register while the seal beside it uses a spring register.
defects.evidence: ActionBarToggle.vue:120-128 — `transition: grid-template-columns var(--duration-normal) var(--ease-standard), opacity …`. The component's own header at :12-16 records that it fires on the app's boot composition ('the pane mounts a beat after the dock, so its action-bar context arrives ~170ms in — the slot visibly GREW the pill on EVERY load'). Everything else in the dock is transform/opacity only: vj-settle = scale(1)→1.03→1 at demo/styles/animations.css:170. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6: 'Spatial continuity uses one producer-owned glass-ui spring register.'
defects.mechanism: grid-template-columns is a layout-animated property; the .is-live double-rAF gate suppresses the visible boot growth but not the layout work on every genuine toggle. Two motion registers in one component (duration/ease on the slot, --spring-snappy on the seal and settle).
defects.reproduction: Read ActionBarToggle.vue:115-128 and demo/styles/animations.css:170; observe the slot transition in DevTools Performance while toggling the Tools presence (navigate picker → browse → picker).
defects.proposedCure: Animate the slot with transform: scaleX() + opacity on a fixed-basis box, or do not animate it at all — a dock control appearing is not a spatial-continuity event. If it stays, it moves onto the producer's spring register so the dock speaks one motion language.

defects.defect: CORRECTION TO r1: r1's strongest BLOCKER ('the dock is keyboard-unreachable on Safari; 1 of 4 controls in the tab order') is a known false-signal class the repository's own harness rules out.
defects.evidence: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/states.mjs:7-9 — 'keyboard rows are meaningless in WebKit alone — macOS ships Full Keyboard Access OFF, so run ENGINE=chromium before believing any focus gap, and key focus identity by DOM path, never by label (see probes/kbd-reach.mjs)'. Independent Chromium reproduction, D-dock-probe1.mjs at 1440x900: tab order = Select view → Toggle action bar → Login → @mbabb → [page] Select color space → …, all four dock controls present and in visual order.
defects.mechanism: Safari's 'Press Tab to highlight each item on a webpage' is a macOS user setting that excludes bare <button> from sequential focus on EVERY site; Playwright's WebKit inherits the OFF default. It is a property of the harness environment, not of this dock.
defects.reproduction: node D-dock-probe1.mjs — Chromium 1440x900, 12 sequential Tab presses from load, logging document.activeElement DOM path + accessible name after each.
defects.proposedCure: Retire the BLOCKER framing so the root does not ship a row no reviewer with FKA enabled can reproduce. KEEP the underlying observation as a MAJOR: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.2 row 6 specifies a horizontal Dock roving-focus rail (Right/Left movement, Home/End, activation separate from movement) and Dock.vue implements zero keyboard handling — the dock is a loose row of independent buttons where the constitution specifies a rail.

defects.defect: Rendered text from three inactive dock layers is present in the nav's innerText/textContent, including a bare '→' and the full specimen colour string.

AT is protected because the faces are inert, but every text-based probe, crawler, snapshot test and bodyTextLength metric reads content from three layers the user cannot see — which is how a shell text metric can move with nothing visible changing.

defects.proposedCure: aria-hidden="true" on the connector arrow at minimum; better, it is a ::before/border between the two WatercolorDots, not a text node. Long-term, the layer set should be v-if'd on activation rather than kept mounted — four always-mounted layers is why three of them are always leaking.

defects.defect: A role="alert" node is mounted permanently in the nav band from first paint, and carries an infinite pulse animation in persistent chrome.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/status-lamp.ts:47-52 returns {variant:"misconfigured", role:"alert", label:"dev misconfigured — run `npm run dev`"}; DockStatusLamp.vue:12-20 renders it with the band. The pulse is correctly wrapped in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference), so PRM users are unaffected, but it is unbounded motion in persistent chrome with no pause control (cf. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6's five-second/pause rule for ambient motion).
defects.reproduction: node D-dock-probe2.mjs — read .dock-status-lamp rect, role and text at 390x844 on /#/ against the dev server; or read status-lamp.ts:47-52.
defects.proposedCure: role="status" for a lamp that exists from first paint (assertive interruption is for a state that CHANGES). Bound the pulse to a finite count, or drop it — a dev-config error does not become more legible by blinking forever.

defects.defect: Two template-ref idioms fourteen lines apart in one file, and two computed properties that only re-spell `?? null`.
defects.evidence: Dock.vue:74 `const dockRef = useTemplateRef<InstanceType<typeof GlassDock>>('dockRef')` (Vue 3.5, per owner edict 7) alongside Dock.vue:60 `const slugEditRef = ref<InstanceType<typeof SlugEditLayer> | null>(null)` for the same job. Dock.vue:39-40 `const actionBar = computed(() => actionBarProp ?? null)` and `const genericBar = computed(() => genericActionBar ?? null)` where both props are already typed `… | null | undefined` (Dock.vue:31).
defects.mechanism: Incremental modernisation without a sweep: useTemplateRef was adopted for the new ref and the old one was left. The computed wrappers are pure indirection (owner edict 3, KISS) — they exist only so template call sites can write `actionBar` instead of `actionBarProp`.
defects.reproduction: Read demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue:39-40, :60, :74.
defects.proposedCure: useTemplateRef for both; delete the two computeds and rename the destructured props. Note the deeper issue the slugEditRef exposes: Dock proxies two child methods (onStartSlugEdit, onCopySlug) from two different menus through a template ref — prop/event/ref triangulation for one action. The Account-Dialog move (D2-04) deletes the ref entirely.

defects.defect: CARRIED AND SHARPENED from r1 D-5: the open view menu has zero visual selected-state marking in either scheme, and the one lawfully coloured row (Palettes) therefore impersonates the selection.
defects.evidence: D-dock-probe7.mjs, both schemes: all 7 options report fontWeight "400", backgroundColor "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" and one <svg> child each (the view icon, not an indicator); only Home carries aria-selected "true". Rendered scratchpad/D-viewmenu-light.png: Home is typographically identical to Browse/Extract/Mix/Generate/Gradient, and the only visually marked row is Palettes (the Q5-sanctioned pastel ramp). Sources: DockViewSelect.vue:97 and :127 set hide-indicator on every SelectItem; :99-109 records that the font-semibold marker was retired.
defects.mechanism: hide-indicator strips the producer's SelectItem indicator gutter and the weight marker was deleted at P4-R4, leaving selection expressed only through aria-selected. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1: 'Selected, failed, pending, withdrawn and disabled states are never color-only' — here selection is not even colour, it is nothing; §4.2's ColorSpaceSelector rule ('deletes hide-indicator and consumes the sole producer SelectItem indicator/gutter') is the same mechanism, unapplied here. Menu rows are also Fraunces (DockViewSelect.vue:91), against §4's 'control or label, INCLUDING dropdown options → Plus Jakarta Sans, non-bold'.
defects.reproduction: node D-dock-probe7.mjs — light and dark contexts at 1440x900, click .view-select-trigger, then read every [role=option]'s aria-selected, computed fontWeight, computed backgroundColor and indicator-child count.
defects.proposedCure: Delete hide-indicator from both SelectItem blocks and consume the producer's indicator gutter — it is scheme-, monochrome- and forced-colors-safe by construction, which no consumer-side marker can be. The Palettes ramp then means 'this destination is about colour', not 'this is where you are'.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law) of `demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue`
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M context). Declared at spawn, not inherited.

Measured absent at 390x844 (mobile) and at 720x450 (= a 1440x900 desktop at 200% browser zoom), present at 1440x900. defects.defect: `btn-interactive` — the class both of the component's long comment blocks credit with hover/press legs, focus register and disabled opacity — matches ZERO CSS rules. The send button has identical computed style at rest, hover, active and focus, and no focus indicator.

result.strongestDefect: L-1 — the product's primary navigation renders with NO LABEL on 7 of its 14 views, because the Select's model value (router-owned, range 14) and its option set (`useDockAdminMode`-owned, range 7) have different owners and nothing constrains them to agree. Proven by three same-matrix screenshots (`browse.png` reads "Browse"; `atmosphere.png` and `admin-users.png` render icon+chevron only) and by reka-ui source (`SelectValue.js:33-42` falls back to `placeholder`, which defaults to `""` and is not passed). (One axis did prove sound and is recorded as L-11: the component reaches the library correctly by not reaching it at all. `grep -rn 'from "(\.\./)*\.\./src' demo/` → no matches; `grep -rn '@src/' demo/shell demo/palettes demo/picker` → no matches; `vite.config.ts:37-50` GENERATES the self-alias set from `package.json#exports` so the seven public specifiers cannot drift; `package.json#exports` declares only the 7 subpaths with no `"."` root and correspondingly `grep -rn 'from "@mkbabb/value.js"' demo/` returns nothing. defects.defect: The dock view-select trigger renders an EMPTY label on 7 of the demo's 14 views: the Select's model value and its option set are owned by different modules with different ranges, so the selected value routinely matches no SelectItem.
defects.evidence: Screenshots, same matrix (safari-desktop-light, 1440 CSS px, isDesktop true): docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/browse.png shows the trigger reading "Browse"; atmosphere.png and admin-users.png show icon+chevron with NO text. Mechanism from source: DockViewSelect.vue:73 renders `<SelectValue v-if="isDesktop" />` with no placeholder; node_modules/reka-ui/dist/Select/SelectValue.js:33-42 computes `selectedLabel` by looking modelValue up in `rootContext.optionsSet` and falling back to "", and `slotText` returns `props.placeholder` (default "", lines 10-14) when the lookup misses. Ranges: `:model-value="currentView"` (Dock.vue:169) has range 14 (viewSchema.ts:30-44); `viewEntries` (Dock.vue:173) has range 7 at a time (useDockAdminMode.ts:26-27,34-40). All three shots also show the "Login" control, i.e. unauthenticated — capture.mjs has no login step (grep for admin|login|auth returns only the five route literals at lines 32-36).
defects.mechanism: split enumeration / no single owner of the navigation taxonomy — the option set and the model value are computed from two different modules
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/atmosphere (or /#/blob or any /#/admin/*) unauthenticated at viewport width >= 1024px. The dock view-select trigger shows its icon and chevron with no visible label. Compare /#/browse, which reads "Browse". Already captured in the harness shots listed above.
defects.proposedCure: Do NOT add a placeholder — that hides it. Make it structurally impossible: derive the option set as `viewsInGroup(activeGroup) ∪ {currentView}` so the model value is an option by construction. Requires the single nav schema of L-2.

defects.defect: Three hand-maintained enumerations of the same 14 view identifiers exist in three directories, and two of them directly contradict each other about what "admin" means.
defects.evidence: (1) demo/shell/viewSchema.ts:30-44 + VIEW_MAP :97-234 — the declared SSOT, 14 ViewIds, and it carries NO grouping field at all. (2) demo/color-picker/router/index.ts:22-37 — 14 routes hand-listed, `meta:{admin:true}` on exactly 5 (:31-35); /atmosphere (:29) and /blob (:30) have no meta. (3) demo/shell/dock/composables/useDockAdminMode.ts:26-27 — `userViews` (7) and `adminViews` (7), where adminViews INCLUDES "atmosphere" and "blob". Router says 5 admin views; the dock says 7. viewSchema.ts's own header claims it exists 'to retire the 4-copy ViewId enumeration'; its accentHueShift comment (:66-79) speaks of 'the nine primary views ... in dock order', a nine the dock has never had.
defects.mechanism: incomplete SSOT — VIEW_MAP lacks the `group` field the dock needs, so the enumeration regrew in a third home
defects.reproduction: grep -n "meta: { admin: true }" demo/color-picker/router/index.ts → 5 hits; sed -n '27p' demo/shell/dock/composables/useDockAdminMode.ts → 7 ids including atmosphere and blob. Adding a view today requires three synchronised edits and nothing fails if you make two.
defects.proposedCure: One home: `demo/shell/nav/nav-schema.ts` — VIEW_MAP gains `group: "primary"|"tuning"|"admin"` and `path`; `routes.ts` DERIVES the route table from it (`Object.entries(VIEW_MAP).map(...)`) so a view cannot exist without a route; the dock reads `viewsInGroup(g)` instead of re-listing ids.

defects.defect: Seven of fourteen views have no UI reachability at all (URL-typing only), and five of them render the full admin console to an unauthenticated visitor because `meta: { admin: true }` has zero readers and no route guard exists.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "meta.admin\|beforeEach\|beforeResolve\|addRoute" demo/ --include='*.ts' --include='*.vue'` → NO OUTPUT. router/index.ts:44-48 registers exactly one guard, installDocumentTitle. Screenshot: shots/safari-desktop-light/admin-users.png renders 'Users · Manage accounts and permissions', a search field, 'Prune empty' and 'Refresh' while the dock control still reads 'Login'. REPORT.md:128-132 records main=1 and 244-273 chars of text for all five admin routes in every matrix, unauthenticated. Reachability: atmosphere/blob/admin-* appear only in adminViews (useDockAdminMode.ts:27), returned only when `isAdminMode && isAdminAuthenticated` (:35); isAdminMode rises only via the `__admin_toggle__` row (rendered under `v-if="pm.isAdminAuthenticated.value"`, DockViewSelect.vue:114) or via the watcher at :55-59 that fires on ALREADY landing there. Admin auth itself has no nav entry — it is a hidden mode of the slug field (useSlugMigration.ts:51-56). MobileMenuDropdown.vue:36-113 carries no view navigation, so mobile has the same hole. No switchView/router.push/href anywhere in demo/ targets atmosphere or blob.
defects.mechanism: the authorization concept has three partial homes (dead router meta, a menu filter, a template v-if) and no owner
defects.reproduction: grep -rn "meta.admin|beforeEach|beforeResolve|addRoute" demo/ --include='*.ts' --include='*.vue' → empty. Then open http://localhost:9000/#/admin/users in a fresh profile: the admin console renders while the dock offers 'Login'.
defects.proposedCure: `demo/shell/nav/guard.ts` — the ONE reader of `meta.group === "admin"`: `router.beforeEach(to => useAdminAuth().isAuthenticated.value || to.meta.group !== "admin" ? true : { name: "picker" })`. Gives the dead metadata its only consumer and makes the menu filter a presentation detail rather than the de-facto gate.

defects.defect: Wrong direction of dependency: the app shell imports from a feature to read platform auth. `demo/shell/dock/DockViewSelect.vue` injects `SESSION_PORT_KEY` from `demo/palettes/usePalettePorts` — a laundering hop to a platform singleton the parent already holds.
defects.evidence: DockViewSelect.vue:8 `import { SESSION_PORT_KEY } from "../../palettes/usePalettePorts"` and :35 `const pm = inject(SESSION_PORT_KEY)!`. Five shell files do this: DockViewSelect.vue:8, Dock.vue:18, layers/SlugEditLayer.vue:5, menus/MobileMenuDropdown.vue:13, menus/ProfileSection.vue:14. The key is named for the wrong domain — `Symbol("palette.session")` at usePalettePorts.ts:271. The feature does not own the value: usePalettePorts.ts:57 does `const { isAuthenticated: isAdminAuthenticated } = useAdminAuth()`, and demo/platform/auth/useAdminAuth.ts:17-24 is a module-level singleton (one lazily created `_adminToken` ref shared by all callers, by design). Worse, Dock.vue:37 injects the SAME key and Dock.vue:44 already passes `pm.isAdminAuthenticated` into useDockAdminMode — the value is one level up and deliberately not passed as a prop.
defects.mechanism: feature-shaped port used as the transport for a platform concern; component is half props-driven, half ambient (dual data path)
defects.reproduction: grep -rn "SESSION_PORT_KEY" demo/ → five demo/shell/** importers of demo/palettes/usePalettePorts. Read DockViewSelect.vue:16-23 (five props) then :35 (a sixth input reached around the prop surface).
defects.proposedCure: Delete the edge. This component takes no auth input at all — Dock.vue passes what the option set needs. Where the shell genuinely needs auth (the future guard), call `useAdminAuth()` from `demo/platform/auth` directly: one hop, correct direction, no inject, no feature dependency. Resulting lattice: platform/auth → shell/nav → shell/dock → glass-ui, with features reading the shell and the shell reading no feature.

defects.defect: Two paths to the same design system inside one file, eight lines apart: `@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock` at line 3 and `../../ui/select` at lines 4-6, where demo/ui/select is a one-line pure re-export of @mkbabb/glass-ui. All 19 demo/ui/* barrels are pure forwards.

defects.defect: `demo/shell/useViewManager.ts` carries a self-declared back-compat type re-export shim preserving compatibility with an import path (`@composables/useViewManager`) that no longer exists, and it is the MAJORITY path for the ViewId family (6 of 9 importers), keeping a dual path alive.

defects.defect: `ViewEntry` is a type-erased duplicate of `PaneConfig & { id: ViewId }`: it re-declares two fields, downgrades `icon: Component` to `icon: unknown`, and opens an `[k: string]: unknown` index signature that makes the type accept anything — forcing an `as` cast at both construction sites and erasing this component's prop contract.
defects.evidence: useDockAdminMode.ts:7-12 `export interface ViewEntry { id: ViewId; label: string; icon: unknown; [k: string]: unknown; }` vs viewSchema.ts:86-96 where `PaneConfig.icon: Component` (typed via `import type { Component } from "vue"`, :15). Casts required at :36 and :38 — `adminViews.map((id) => ({ id, ...viewManager.viewMap[id] } as ViewEntry))`. Erasure propagates into the public prop surface: DockViewSelect.vue:16 `currentIcon: unknown` and :22 `viewEntries: ViewEntry[]`, both then fed to `<component :is>` at :66 and :97 — a position vue-tsc does not check, so the props assert nothing about the one thing the component renders. `grep -rn "ViewEntry" demo/` → 7 hits, confined to these two files. Ownership inversion in the import itself: DockViewSelect.vue:9 takes its PROP TYPE from a composable rather than the schema.
defects.mechanism: a second, weaker type for a concept the schema already owns — duplicate ownership plus deliberate type erasure
defects.reproduction: sed -n '7,12p' demo/shell/dock/composables/useDockAdminMode.ts vs sed -n '86,96p' demo/shell/viewSchema.ts.
defects.proposedCure: Delete `ViewEntry`. Use `PaneConfig & { id: ViewId }` from the nav schema — same shape, fully typed, already exported, no cast at either construction site, and the component's prop type stops depending on a stateful composable.

defects.defect: The view-change channel carries two disjoint meanings — a ViewId and the magic sentinel `"__admin_toggle__"` — and the far end casts unvalidated into `router.push` while the type predicate written for exactly that check is never called on the write path.
defects.evidence: DockViewSelect.vue:105 `<SelectItem value="__admin_toggle__" ...>`. useDockAdminMode.ts:65-73: `function onViewChange(id: string | number | boolean | Record<string, string> | null) { if (typeof id === "string") { if (id === "__admin_toggle__") { toggleAdminMode(); return; } viewManager.switchView(id as ViewId); } }` — the cast lands in `router.push({ name: id })` at useViewManager.ts:79. viewSchema.ts:236 exports `isViewId`, and `grep -rn "isViewId" demo/` shows it used only on the READ path (useViewManager.ts:45, useDocumentTitle.ts:50). Doubled defensive typing that validates nothing: DockViewSelect.vue:80 already narrows with `emit('update:modelValue', id as string)` and declares the emit `[id: string]` at :26, yet the receiver re-widens to reka's full AcceptableValue union.
defects.mechanism: one channel, two message types (navigate | toggle-mode) plus an unchecked cast at the module boundary
defects.reproduction: sed -n '65,73p' demo/shell/dock/composables/useDockAdminMode.ts; grep -rn "isViewId" demo/ shows no call site on the write path.
defects.proposedCure: Split the channel: `emits: { navigate: [ViewId]; toggleAdmin: [] }`. Type `switchView(id: ViewId)` and let callers narrow with `isViewId` — no cast, no sentinel, no magic string with no home.

defects.defect: `demo/shell/dock/index.ts` forms a genuine ESM module cycle with `Dock.vue`, and the barrel is a contrivance: it re-exports three glass-ui symbols for exactly one consumer, which is itself a member of the barrel.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/index.ts in full (5 lines): `export { GlassDock, DockLayerGroup, DockLayer } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock";` + `export { default as Dock } from "./Dock.vue";`. demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue:4: `import { GlassDock, DockLayerGroup, DockLayer } from "./";`. Cycle: index.ts → Dock.vue → index.ts. The barrel's only external value is `Dock`, imported once at demo/color-picker/App.vue:167.
defects.mechanism: alias barrel adding no value while creating a dependency cycle (same class as L-5)
defects.reproduction: cat demo/shell/dock/index.ts && sed -n '4p' demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the file. Dock.vue imports `@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock` directly; App.vue imports `../shell/dock/Dock.vue`. Removes the cycle and the alias in one stroke.

defects.defect: One two-way binding is spelled three times: `defineModel("open")`, a redundant explicit `"update:open"` entry in `defineEmits`, and hand-wired `:open` / `@update:open` instead of `v-model:open`.
defects.evidence: DockViewSelect.vue:24-33 declares `const emit = defineEmits<{ "update:modelValue": [id: string]; "update:open": [open: boolean]; }>();` immediately followed by `const open = defineModel<boolean>("open", { default: false });` — defineModel generates the `update:open` emit itself in Vue 3.4+, so the explicit entry is a duplicate declaration and dead. Then :38-39 hand-wires `:open="open"` and `@update:open="open = $event"`, which is what `v-model:open="open"` means.
defects.mechanism: three spellings of one binding — redundant declaration plus manual re-implementation of a framework idiom
defects.reproduction: sed -n '24,39p' demo/shell/dock/DockViewSelect.vue.
defects.proposedCure: Keep `defineModel`, drop the `"update:open"` line from defineEmits, and use `v-model:open="open"` on `<Select>` (idiomatic Vue 3.5, standing edict 7).
